gaps.sentence: She decided ___ the job offer in Berlin.
gaps.explanation: decide takes the to-infinitive: decided to accept.

gaps.sentence: I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.

gaps.sentence: We managed ___ everyone before the storm hit.
I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
She was the first woman ___ the peak in winter.
gaps.explanation: the first/second/last + to-infinitive: the first woman to climb.

gaps.sentence: I can't imagine ___ in a tiny village again.
We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.

gaps.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)
